sentences.text:
Cra No. 2601 of 2008
 (Umrao Vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh
 Dated : 26-03-2026

Shri Kapil Pathak, Advocate for appellant.
 Shri Mukesh Shukla, Govt. Advocate for respondent-Stat
The appeal is already admitted on 05.01.2009.
Heard on I.A.No.6305/2026, which is fourth application filed on behalf of appellant under Section 389(1) of the Cr.P.C./Section 430 of BNSS for suspension of sentence and grant of bail.

The appellant has been convicted by the trial Court under Section 450 of IPC and sentenced to undergo R.I. for 7 years with fine of Rs.500/-, Section 376 of IPC and sentenced to undergo R.I. for 7 years with fine of Rs.500/- and under Section 323 of IPC and sentenced to undergo R.I. for 1 year with fine of Rs. 500/- with default stipulation in each.
Learned counsel for the appellant submits that previously the appellant was granted bail vide order dtd. 13.03.2012.
In pursuance of order dtd. 21.07.2025, the appellant has been taken into custody and is in custody since 14.10.2025.
He further submits that Trial Court has not properly appreciated the oral and documentary evidence available on record while convicting the appellant for the aforesaid offences.
It is contended by the counsel that as of now, the appellant has already suffered about four and half years of incarceration.
There is material contradictions and omissions in the evidence of witnesses.
There is fair chance to succeed in the appeal.
Under these circumstances, if the sentence of the appellant is not suspended, purpose to file this appeal will be futile.

Therefore,
prayer is 2 CRA-2601-2008 made for suspension of execution of jail sentence and grant of bail of present appellant.

Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent opposed the prayer and submits that the appellant has been rightly convicted by the trial Court on the basis of proper appreciation of oral as well as documentary evidence.
Therefore, sentence of the appellant should not be suspended.
Heard the submissions and perused the record.

sentences.text: Taking into consideration the aforesaid and the fact that appellant has already suffered about four and half years of incarceration and was already granted bail vide order dtd. 13.03.2012, this Court deems it proper to enlarge the appellant on bail.
Therefore, I.A.No.6305/2026 is allowed.

It is directed that subject to depositing the fine amount, if not already deposited and on furnishing a personal bond in a sum of Rs.20,000/- (Rupees Twenty Thousand only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Trial Court concerned, the custodial sentence of the appellant shall remain suspended and he shall be released on bail for securing his presence before the Trial Court concerned on 12.10.2026 and on such other dates, as may be fixed by that Court in this regard during pendency of this appeal.
List the matter for final hearing in due course.
Certified copy as per rules.
